s: Which shipyard built INS Vikrant (IAC-1), India's first indigenous aircraft carrier?
x: INS Vikrant, India's first indigenous aircraft carrier (IAC-1), was built by Cochin Shipyard.

s: Which submarine is identified as the last boat of Project 75?
x: Vaghsheer is the last P75 boat. (Surat is the last P15B destroyer, H-561 the first indigenous hovercraft, and INS Tamal was built in Russia.)

s: Which destroyer is the fourth and last of Project 15B?
x: Surat (2025) is the 4th and last P15B Visakhapatnam-class destroyer.

s: Where was INS Tamal, commissioned on 1 July 2025, built?
x: INS Tamal was built abroad at the Yantar Shipyard, Kaliningrad, Russia.

s: With INS Arihant, India became which country in the world to have armed nuclear submarine (SSBN) capability?
x: INS Arihant, inducted in August 2016, made India the 6th country with this capability.

s: What is INS Arihant?
o: Indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel
x: INS Arihant is India’s first SSBN, or nuclear ballistic-missile submarine, commissioned in 2016.

s: When was INS Vikrant, India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, commissioned?
x: INS Vikrant (IAC-1) was commissioned by the PM at Cochin Shipyard on 2 September 2022.

s: When was the stealth frigate Tavasya launched at Goa Shipyard?
x: Tavasya was launched in March 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indian naval ship projects?
o: INS Surat is the fourth and last ship of Project 15B
Project 17A consists of seven stealth destroyers
x: Project 17A consists of seven Nilgiri-class stealth frigates, not destroyers.

s: Under which project are the Kalvari-class Scorpene submarines built?
x: The Kalvari class belongs to Project 75: six French-design Scorpene diesel-electric submarines, the last being INS Vaghsheer.

s: With which Indian firm did Navantia of Spain sign a teaming agreement in July 2023 for Project-75(I) AIP-equipped submarines?
x: Project-75(I) concerns next-generation conventional submarines with air-independent propulsion; Navantia and L&T signed a teaming agreement in July 2023.

s: Where were the three vessels INS Cheetah, INS Guldar and INS Kumbhir decommissioned on 12 January 2024?
x: INS Cheetah, Guldar and Kumbhir were decommissioned on 12 January 2024 at Port Blair.

s: With which of the following is Tavasya associated?
o: An indigenously built stealth frigate launched by the Navy, belonging to the P-1135.6 follow-on project at Goa Shipyard
A Nilgiri-class frigate constructed at GRSE under Project 17A
A Scorpene submarine built at MDL under Project-75
A Kamorta-class corvette built at Cochin Shipyard
x: Tavasya is an indigenously built stealth frigate launched by the Navy, associated with the P-1135.6 follow-on project at Goa Shipyard.

s: Which ships are built under Project 17A?
x: P17A builds Nilgiri-class frigates, not destroyers; P15B is the destroyer project.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: P28 is the Kamorta-class corvette project; P15B = destroyers, P17A = frigates, P75 = submarines.

s: How many stealth frigates are being built under Project 17A?
x: Project 17A has seven Nilgiri-class stealth frigates, built by MDL and GRSE.

s: Which type of submarine was INS Sindhurakshak, which sank after a fire at the Mumbai dockyard on 14 Aug 2013?
x: INS Sindhurakshak was a Russian Kilo-class submarine.

s: Which P17A frigate, the seventh of the class, joined the Eastern Fleet on 18 July 2026?
x: Mahendragiri, the 7th P17A frigate, joined the Eastern Fleet on 18 July 2026.

s: Where was INS Imphal, a Project 15B stealth destroyer, commissioned on 26 December 2023?
x: INS Imphal, the third P15B (Visakhapatnam-class) destroyer, was commissioned at Mumbai on 26 December 2023.

s: Which Indian Navy hydrographic survey ship has been fitted with solar panels as a green initiative?
x: INS Sarvekshak, a hydrographic survey ship, was fitted with solar panels as a green initiative.

s: Which AESA radar is fitted on the Nilgiri-class (Project 17A) stealth frigates?
x: The P17A frigates carry the MF-STAR AESA radar along with BrahMos and MRSAM.

s: Where was the Project 17A frigate Taragiri commissioned in April 2026?
x: Taragiri was commissioned at Visakhapatnam in April 2026.

s: Which shipyards are building the Nilgiri-class frigates?
x: The Nilgiri-class Project 17A frigates are being built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders and Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers.

s: How many Rafale fighter jets from Dassault does the Indian Air Force operate?
x: The IAF operates 36 Rafales; 26 is the number of Rafale-M jets ordered for the Navy.

s: What is the role of the IL-76 in the Indian Air Force?
x: The Russian IL-76 is a heavy transport, not a combat aircraft; the IL-78 is the refuelling tanker.

s: How many Rafale-M aircraft have been ordered for the Indian Navy?
x: 26 Rafale-M have been ordered for the Navy; the IAF has 36 Rafales.

s: What is the role of the Boeing C-17 Globemaster III in IAF service?
x: The C-17 Globemaster III from Boeing, USA, is a strategic heavy-lift aircraft.

s: Where is the Dornier Do-228 licence-built in India?
x: The German Dornier Do-228 is licence-built by HAL at Kanpur for maritime patrol and light transport.

s: Which company of the USA makes the C-130J tactical transport aircraft used by the IAF?
x: The C-130J Super Hercules is made by Lockheed Martin; India bought it in a 2008 deal of about $1.1 billion.

s: The Tejas Mk-1A carries which indigenous AESA radar?
x: Tejas Mk-1A has the Uttam AESA radar, an EW suite and air-to-air refuelling.

s: The Netra AEW&C system built by DRDO-CABS, Bengaluru, is mounted on which aircraft?
x: Netra carries an AESA radar on an Embraer EMB-145, with a detection range of about 250–500+ km.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about AWACS and the Netra AEW&C system?
o: AWACS is mounted on a smaller jet than Netra
Netra is mounted on a smaller jet than AWACS
Netra provides early warning and command-and-control
AWACS has a longer range than Netra
x: Netra is the smaller jet; AWACS is larger, with longer range and full air-battle control.

s: Of which phenomenon is the changing pitch of a passing siren an example?
x: It is the Doppler effect, also used in radar guns, medical Doppler and astronomy (with light).

s: Which of the following radar pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Doppler radar – Speed from frequency shift
AESA radar – T/R module on every element, beam steered electronically
Over-the-horizon radar – Imaging at night and through clouds
x: Over-the-horizon radar bounces HF waves off the ionosphere; imaging at night and through clouds is SAR.

s: In medical ultrasound, what is measured using the frequency-shift (Doppler) technique?
x: Medical ultrasound measures blood-flow velocity, just as weather radar detects wind speed and SONAR tracks underwater objects.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Doppler effect in astronomy?
o: The Doppler effect is used to study the motion of stars
A red shift of starlight shows that the star is approaching
A blue shift of starlight shows that the star is approaching
Red shift and blue shift of starlight are Doppler shifts
x: A red shift means the star is moving away; a blue shift means it is approaching.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Doppler effect?
o: It is an apparent change in frequency caused by relative motion
An approaching source shows a higher apparent frequency
An approaching sound source sounds lower in pitch
It explains the changing pitch of a passing siren
x: An approaching source sounds higher in pitch, not lower; the Doppler effect is a frequency change from relative motion.

s: Which type of radar produces images at night and through clouds?
x: SAR images at night and through clouds.

s: How does over-the-horizon radar work?
o: Bouncing HF waves off the ionosphere
Using long VHF waves to pick up stealth aircraft
Placing a T/R module on every element
Measuring the frequency shift of echoes
x: Over-the-horizon radar bounces HF waves off the ionosphere.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radar types?
o: SAR produces images at night and through clouds
AESA radar uses a mechanically rotating antenna
VHF anti-stealth radar uses long waves
AESA has a T/R module on every element
x: AESA steers its beam electronically with no moving antenna.

s: What is Ashwini?
o: Fire-control radar of the Akash system
Low-level lightweight 3D radar detecting cruise missiles and drones
x: Ashwini is a low-level lightweight 3D radar that detects cruise missiles and drones; Swathi is weapon-locating, Rajendra serves Akash and Swordfish does long-range tracking.

s:
Consider the following statements about indigenous radars:
1. Swordfish is the long-range tracking radar of the BMD shield.
2. Rajendra is the fire-control radar of the Akash SAM system.
3. Surya is the fire-control radar of the Akash SAM system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Swordfish tracks for the BMD shield and Rajendra is Akash's fire-control radar; Surya is the VHF radar for tracking stealth aircraft.

s: What type of radar is the IAF's Arudhra?
x: Arudhra is an IAF medium-power 4D, 360° surveillance radar of 300+ km.

s: To which country has the Swathi weapon-locating radar, made by BEL, been exported?
x: BEL's Swathi weapon-locating radar has been exported to Armenia.

s: Which indigenous radar tracks stealth aircraft?
x: Surya is the VHF radar for tracking stealth aircraft.

s: For what is INDRA (Indian Doppler Radar) used?
x: INDRA is a low-level surveillance radar.

s: For what is the Swathi radar made by BEL used?
o: Locating enemy guns, mortars and rockets
Fire control of the Akash missile
x: Swathi is a weapon-locating radar that finds the position of enemy guns, mortars and rockets.

s: What does the radar cross-section (RCS) of a target indicate?
o: The maximum range of the radar
How big the target looks to radar
The frequency at which the radar operates
x: RCS is how 'big' a target looks to radar; shaping, radar-absorbent coatings and flush-mounted weapons reduce it.

s: Which institute has developed a low-cost radar-absorbing metamaterial to cloak soldiers and equipment from enemy radar?
x: IIT Kharagpur developed a low-cost radar-absorbing metamaterial that hides soldiers and equipment from radar.

s: In which year was DRDO, whose motto is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam', formed?
x: DRDO was formed in 1958 and its motto is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' (the source of strength is science).

s: Which of the following do the SAGAR and MAHASAGAR visions guide in India?
x: The SAGAR and MAHASAGAR visions guide India's maritime and naval capabilities.

s: Where did the Navy set up the Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) in 2018?
x: IFC-IOR is at Gurugram and shares white-shipping and maritime-security data with partner countries.

s: Where is a new submarine base for the Eastern Naval Command being built?
x: The new submarine base is at Rambilli; INS Dega is the naval air station and Visakhapatnam is the ENC headquarters.

s: Which city hosts the Eastern Naval Command, Hindustan Shipyard Limited and NSTL?
x: Visakhapatnam hosts the Eastern Naval Command, HSL and NSTL (linked with Varunastra).

s: What is INS Dega at Visakhapatnam?
x: INS Dega is the naval air station at Visakhapatnam; the new submarine base is at Rambilli.

s: How often is the Naval Commanders' Conference held?
x: The Naval Commanders' Conference is held twice a year; the first 2024 edition began on 5 March 2024.

s: Near which city of Andhra Pradesh is a DRDO test range located?
x: Besides the Visakhapatnam defence units, DRDO has a test range near Kurnool in Andhra Pradesh.

s: In which category is Tejas India's first indigenous aircraft?
x: Tejas is identified as India's first indigenous fly-by-wire aircraft.

s: Which agency designed the Tejas Light Combat Aircraft, built by HAL?
x: The Tejas LCA was designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency and built by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited.

s: How many LCA Mk1A aircraft does HAL's 2025 contract cover?
x: The 25 September 2025 contract covers 97 aircraft (68 fighters and 29 twin-seaters); it followed an earlier order of 83 Mk1A.

s: Which engine powers the Tejas Mk-2, now under development with canards?
x: Tejas Mk-2 uses the GE F414 engine; the sequence of variants is Mk-1, Mk-1A, then Mk-2.

s: What type of aircraft is the C-295, built by Airbus (Spain) with Tata?
x: The C-295 is a medium tactical transport; the C-17 is the strategic heavy-lift transport. The first Made-in-India C-295 rolls out in 2026.

s: Who developed the LCH Prachand, a light combat helicopter for high altitude?
x: LCH Prachand is a HAL light combat helicopter for high-altitude operations.

s: What is the HTT-40, developed by HAL?
x: HTT-40 is HAL's basic turboprop trainer.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Tejas Light Combat Aircraft:
1. It is a 4.5-generation light multirole supersonic fighter.
2. It has a compound delta-wing, tailless design.
3. It is a twin-engine fighter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Tejas is a 4.5-generation, tailless compound delta-wing fighter, but it has a single engine.

s: Who named the Tejas fighter?
x: Tejas was named by Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

s:
Consider the following statements about Dhruv:
1. It is a twin-engine Advanced Light Helicopter made by HAL.
2. It is used only by the Indian Army.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Dhruv is HAL's twin-engine Advanced Light Helicopter used by all three services and the Coast Guard, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: What is LLM-105?
x: LLM-105 is an insensitive high explosive with greater safety against accidental detonation.

s:
Consider the following statements about CL-20:
1. It is associated with HEMRL, Pune.
2. It is described as the most powerful non-nuclear explosive.
3. It is associated with TBRL, Chandigarh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: CL-20 is associated with the High Energy Materials Research Laboratory (HEMRL), Pune, and is the most powerful non-nuclear explosive; it is not a TBRL product.

s: Which of the following is the formula of TNT?
x: TNT (trinitrotoluene) is C₆H₂(NO₂)₃CH₃, that is C₇H₅N₃O₆. C₃H₆N₆O₆ is RDX, C₆H₃N₃O₇ picric acid and C₃H₅(ONO₂)₃ nitroglycerine.

s: By what name is trinitrophenol commonly known?
x: Trinitrophenol is picric acid; trinitroglycerine is Nobel's oil, RDX cyclonite and HMX octogen.

s: By what other name is the explosive CL-20 known?
x: CL-20 is HNIW; HMX is High Melting Explosive.

s: What is RDX chemically?
x: RDX is cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine; TNP is trinitrophenol and TNG is glyceryl trinitrate.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: RDX is (O₂NNCH₂)₃. TNG is C₃H₅(ONO₂)₃, TNP is (O₂N)₃C₆H₂OH and CL-20 is C₆H₆N₁₂O₁₂.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Dynamite consists of nitroglycerine absorbed in sawdust or kieselguhr.
Blasting gelatin contains 91–93% nitroglycerine, 6–8% nitrocellulose and about 1% acid acceptor.
C-4 consists of HMX in a plastic matrix.
Amatol is composed of TNT and ammonium nitrate.
x: Option C is incorrect: C-4 plastic explosive is based on RDX, not HMX. The dynamite, blasting gelatin and amatol compositions are right.

s: Which explosive is also used in printing inks, leather finishing and celluloid?
x: Gun cotton is used in printing inks, leather finishing and celluloid; picric acid (TNP) is used in explosives and dyes.

s: Amatol is a mixture of TNT and which of the following?
x: Amatol is TNT mixed with ammonium nitrate; it contains no nitroglycerine and is a high explosive, not a propellant.

s:
Assertion (A): Cordite contains nitroglycerine.
Reason (R): Cordite is a propellant.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: cordite is a nitroglycerine–nitrocellulose propellant; its use does not explain what it contains.

s: By what other name is HMX known?
x: HMX is Octogen (High Melting Explosive); Cyclonite and Hexogen are RDX, HNIW is CL-20.

s:
Consider the following statements about explosive mixtures:
1. Dynamite is nitroglycerine in kieselguhr or sawdust.
2. Blasting gelatin is nitroglycerine with nitrocellulose.
3. Amatol contains nitroglycerine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Dynamite and blasting gelatin contain nitroglycerine; Amatol is TNT with ammonium nitrate and has no nitroglycerine.

s: Cyclonite, hexogen and T-4 are alternative names of which explosive?
x: Cyclonite, hexogen and T-4 are names of RDX; octogen is HMX.

s: What is the primary agent in C-4 plastic explosive?
x: RDX is the base of C-4; TNT fills shells and bombs, and amatol is a high explosive.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of gun cotton?
o: Nitroglycerine absorbed in sawdust or kieselguhr
Cotton or wood fibres treated with HNO₃ and H₂SO₄
x: Gun cotton is cotton or wood cellulose nitrated with a mixture of HNO₃ and H₂SO₄. TNT with ammonium nitrate is amatol and RDX in plastic is C-4.

s: Which Indian shipyard was the first Indian yard to export a warship, sending one to Mauritius in 2014?
x: GRSE was the first Indian shipyard to export a warship; the export to Mauritius took place in 2014.

s: Of which type is the Coast Guard's Hovercraft H-561 (2026) India's first indigenous vessel?
x: H-561 is the first indigenous air cushion vehicle and can work over mudflats and sandbars such as the Rann of Kutch and the Sundarbans.

s: Which shipyard built Jala Usha (1948), the first Indian-built ship?
x: Jala Usha, the first Indian-built ship (1948), came from Hindustan Shipyard, Visakhapatnam.

s: Under which initiative was India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel cell ferry, flagged off in February 2024, built?
x: The hydrogen fuel cell ferry built by Cochin Shipyard is part of the Harit Nauka initiative for green inland vessels.

s: From which city did the Prime Minister virtually flag off India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel cell ferry on 28 February 2024?
x: The PM flagged off the Cochin Shipyard-built ferry virtually from Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu; the ferry is meant for Varanasi.

s: Which Mumbai-based shipyard builds destroyers, P17A frigates and Scorpene submarines?
x: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, Mumbai builds destroyers, Project 17A frigates and Scorpene submarines.

s: Which of the following shipyards is under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways?
x: Only Cochin Shipyard (builder of INS Vikrant) is under that ministry; HSL, MDL, GRSE and Goa Shipyard are Ministry of Defence PSUs.

s: Who founded Hindustan Shipyard, Visakhapatnam, in 1941?
x: Hindustan Shipyard was founded in 1941 by Scindia Steam Navigation; it is now an MoD PSU.

s: Where is GRSE, a Defence PSU that has built 118 warships, located?
x: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) is at Kolkata.

s: Where is Goa Shipyard, which builds the Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessels, located?
x: Goa Shipyard, a Defence PSU, is at Vasco da Gama.

s: In which year was the Indian Coast Guard set up?
x: The ICG dates from 1977; its 84 coastal radar stations were set up after 26/11.

s: Which shipyard is building the Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessels?
x: Goa Shipyard is building eight Adamya-class FPVs for coastal surveillance, anti-smuggling and search and rescue.

s: How many radar stations form the Indian Coast Guard's coastal radar chain set up after 26/11?
x: The Coast Guard has 84 radar stations in the coastal radar chain set up after 26/11.

s: How many Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessels are being built for the Coast Guard?
x: Goa Shipyard is building eight Adamya-class FPVs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indian Coast Guard?
o: Search and rescue is one of its roles
Its Adamya-class FPVs are built by GRSE
x: The Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessels are built by Goa Shipyard, not GRSE.

s: What type of vessels are the Adamya-class ships of the Indian Coast Guard?
x: The Adamya class are Fast Patrol Vessels; eight are being built for the Coast Guard by Goa Shipyard.

s: Vishwast, inducted into the Indian Coast Guard on 17 March 2010, was the first of a new class of which type of vessel?
x: ICGS Vishwast, built by Goa Shipyard, was the first of a new class of offshore patrol vessels.

s: Which shipyard builds the Samarth-class offshore patrol vessels of the Indian Coast Guard?
x: Samarth-class OPVs are built by Goa Shipyard for the Indian Coast Guard.

s: Which of the following pairs of Indian Coast Guard vessel class and builder is correctly matched?
x: Rajshree-class patrol vessels are built by GRSE, Kolkata; Vikram class by L&T Kattupalli and Samarth class by Goa Shipyard.

s: With which company is DRDO developing the Zorawar light tank for high-altitude areas?
x: Zorawar is developed by DRDO with L&T; Arjun Mk-1A is from CVRDE, Chennai.

s: Which organisation designed ATAGS, the 155 mm/52-calibre towed gun?
x: ATAGS is DRDO-ARDE's indigenous design with industry; Dhanush is the Bofors-based gun from OFB Jabalpur.

s: With which country did NIBE develop Suryastra, a 300 km-range universal rocket launcher?
x: Suryastra is a universal rocket launcher developed by NIBE with Israel, with a stated range of 300 km.

s: What is PINAKA?
o: An Indian multi-barrel rocket launcher developed by DRDO
A Russian-origin main battle tank licence-built at Avadi
A light combat helicopter built by HAL
x: Pinaka is a multi-barrel rocket launcher (MBRL) developed by DRDO (ARDE Pune with HEMRL), as keyed in APPSC 2018. The T-90 Bhishma is the licence-built Russian tank, Astra is the BVR air-to-air missile, and Prachand is HAL's light combat helicopter.

s: Which organisation makes Dhanush, the Bofors-based 155 mm gun?
x: Dhanush is Bofors-based and made by OFB Jabalpur; ATAGS is the DRDO-ARDE gun.

s: Who developed Akashteer, an air-defence control network?
x: Akashteer is an air-defence control network by BEL with the Army.

s: Which DRDO laboratory developed the Arjun Mk-1A main battle tank?
x: Arjun Mk-1A, a third-generation MBT, is from DRDO's CVRDE, Chennai.

s: What is the range of the Pinaka LRGR-120, first test-fired at ITR Chandipur on 29 Dec 2025?
x: Pinaka LRGR-120 had its maiden test on 29 Dec 2025 with a range of 120 km.

s: Where is the T-90 Bhishma tank of Russian origin licence-built?
x: The T-90 Bhishma is licence-built at Heavy Vehicles Factory, Avadi.

s: What is Rustom-II / TAPAS-BH-201?
x: Rustom-II/TAPAS-BH-201 is a MALE UAV; Nishant is tactical, Lakshya a target drone and Ghatak a stealth UCAV.

s: What is Lakshya, developed by DRDO-ADE?
x: Lakshya is a pilotless target drone of DRDO-ADE.

s: Which of the following UAV – class pairs is correctly matched?
x: Ghatak is the stealth flying-wing UCAV; Lakshya is a target drone, Nishant tactical and Rustom-II a MALE UAV.

s: Which laboratory designed Varunastra, an indigenous heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo?
x: Varunastra was designed by NSTL, Visakhapatnam.

s: What is Maareech, an Indian naval system?
x: Maareech is an anti-torpedo decoy; TAL is a lightweight torpedo, USHUS a submarine sonar and ERASR an anti-submarine rocket.

s: On which technology is the DRDO-NMRL Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) system for submarines based?
x: The NMRL system uses fuel cells, letting a diesel-electric submarine stay submerged for long periods without snorkelling.

s: What is USHUS?
x: USHUS is an integrated submarine sonar; Maareech is the anti-torpedo decoy.

s: What is TAL, launched from helicopters such as the MH-60R and from the P-8I?
x: TAL is a lightweight torpedo; Varunastra is the heavyweight one.

s: What does the Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) system allow a diesel-electric submarine to do?
o: Run on a pressurised light-water reactor
x: AIP, a DRDO-NMRL fuel-cell system, keeps a diesel-electric submarine submerged longer without snorkelling.

s: Where was INS Astradharini, India's first indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel, commissioned in 2015?
x: INS Astradharini was commissioned on 6 Oct 2015 at Visakhapatnam.

s: What is the full form of SMART, a torpedo-delivery system under trials?
o: Supersonic Missile Assisted Release of Torpedo
x: SMART stands for Supersonic Missile Assisted Release of Torpedo.

s: Which DRDO laboratory developed ERASR, the anti-submarine rocket tried from INS Kavaratti?
x: ERASR, an anti-submarine rocket, comes from ARDE Pune; its trials were held from INS Kavaratti.

s: Which DRDO laboratory makes the load-bearing stealth structures referred to in stealth technology?
x: ASL makes load-bearing stealth structures.

s: Kanchan armour, the composite armour used on the Arjun tank, was developed by which DRDO laboratory?
x: Kanchan composite armour for the Arjun tank was developed by the Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory (DMRL), Hyderabad, named after Kanchanbagh where DMRL is located. HEMRL Pune synthesised CL-20, TBRL works on HMX/RDX, and CVRDE Chennai designed the Arjun tank itself, not its armour.

s: Which of the following material–application pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Kanchan armour – Composite armour for the Arjun tank
Carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites – Re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles
Super-alloys and tungsten heavy alloys – Engines and penetrator rods
Maraging steel – Re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles
x: Maraging steel is used in rocket motor casings and submarine hulls; heat shields and nozzles use carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites.

s: With which DRDO laboratory are carbon-carbon and C-SiC composites for heat shields and nozzles associated?
x: Carbon-carbon / C-SiC composites come from ASL Hyderabad.

s: For what is maraging steel mainly used?
x: Maraging steel is used in rocket casings and submarine hulls.

s: The Bukhari space heater and Cognobar were developed by which DRDO laboratory?
x: They are DIPAS products; DIHAR, Leh works on high-altitude agriculture and herbal products.

s: Which organisation has adopted bio-digester-based bio-toilets, developed to treat waste in high-altitude areas?
x: Bio-toilets treat waste in high-altitude environments and have been adopted by the Railways.

s: What is Lukoskin, a DRDO product?
x: Lukoskin is a polyherbal ointment used for leucoderma, also called vitiligo.

s: With which partner did INMAS develop 2-DG, the anti-COVID oral drug?
x: 2-DG was developed by INMAS with Dr Reddy's; DCGI gave emergency use in May 2021.

s: Which of the following product – laboratory pairs is correctly matched?
x: OxyCare is from DEBEL; Lukoskin is DIHAR's, 2-DG is INMAS's and the Bukhari heater is DIPAS's.

s: On what does DIHAR, Leh, mainly work?
x: DIHAR does high-altitude agriculture and herbal products; DIPAS covers high-altitude physiology.

s: What is a drone that loiters over an area and then crashes into its target carrying a warhead called?
x: That is a kamikaze drone; the DAC approved jet-based kamikaze drones in July 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements about anti-drone and loitering systems:
1. Indrajaal is an AI-powered anti-drone grid by a Hyderabad start-up.
2. Vayu Astra fires 64 micro-rockets at drone swarms.
3. D4 is a DRDO system with radar, jamming and laser kill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Vayu Astra is NIBE Ltd's loitering munition; it is Bhargavastra that fires 64 micro-rockets.

s: Who developed the D4 anti-drone system, with radar, jamming and laser kill?
x: D4 is DRDO's anti-drone system; it detects at 4 km and kills within 1 km.

s: What is the Army's Samyukta?
x: Samyukta is the Army's mobile integrated ground electronic warfare system.

s:
Consider the following statements about electronic warfare and anti-drone systems:
1. Samyukta is the Army's mobile integrated ground EW system.
2. Himshakti, for mountain terrain, is from DLRL Hyderabad.
3. Akash Tarang is a laser hard-kill system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Samyukta and Himshakti are correctly described; Akash Tarang is an EW soft-kill system that jams control signals.

s: What type of anti-drone system is Akash Tarang, approved by the DAC in July 2026?
o: EW soft-kill system that jams control signals
x: Akash Tarang is an anti-drone EW soft-kill system that jams control signals.

s: Which anti-drone system fires 64 micro-rockets at drone swarms?
x: Bhargavastra is a counter-drone system that fires 64 micro-rockets at drone swarms; Vayu Astra is a loitering munition.

s: How often is the Naval Commanders' Conference held?
x: The conference is held twice a year; its first 2024 edition began on 5 March 2024.

s: Where is the biennial Aero India show held?
x: Aero India is biennial at Yelahanka; DefExpo 2020 was at Lucknow and DefExpo 2022 at Gandhinagar.

s: What period does RAKSHA (Sep 2026), the Defence Minister's roadmap for global defence partnerships, cover?
x: RAKSHA is a 10-year roadmap; its pillars include indigenous exports and maritime security.

s:
Consider the following statements about defence expos:
1. Aero India is held at Yelahanka AFS, Bengaluru.
2. DefExpo is held every year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Aero India is at Yelahanka, Bengaluru; DefExpo, like Aero India, is biennial.

s: Samudra Laksamana is a naval exercise between India and which country?
x: Samudra Laksamana is the India–Malaysia naval exercise.

s: Off which port was the 3rd edition of Samudra Laksamana (28 Feb – 2 Mar 2024) held?
x: It was held off Visakhapatnam with INS Kiltan and KD Lekir.

s: In which year was the first DefExpo held?
x: DefExpo, a biennial expo, was first held in 1999.

s: DefExpo 2022 at Gandhinagar was which edition of the expo?
x: DefExpo 2022 (18–22 Oct, Gandhinagar, 'Path to Pride') was the 12th edition.

s: What was the theme of DefExpo 2020, held at Lucknow?
o: India: The Emerging Defence Manufacturing Hub
The Runway to a Billion Opportunities
Make in India for the World
x: DefExpo 2020 at Lucknow had the theme 'India: The Emerging Defence Manufacturing Hub'; 'Path to Pride' was DefExpo 2022.

s: In which state was DefExpo 2018 held?
x: DefExpo 2018 was held near Chennai, Tamil Nadu; 2020 was at Lucknow and 2022 at Gandhinagar.

s: In July 2023, L&T signed a Teaming Agreement in New Delhi with which company to bid for the P-75(I) submarines?
x: L&T teamed up with Spain's Navantia for the P-75(I) bid.

s: From defence-industrial cooperation between India and which country did the K9 Vajra-T self-propelled gun emerge?
x: The K9 Vajra-T self-propelled gun emerged from India–South Korea cooperation under the 2020 Roadmap for Defence Industries Cooperation.

s: Where is Bharat Forge establishing India's first private marine gas turbine MRO facility?
x: Bharat Forge is setting up India's first private marine gas turbine MRO facility at Visakhapatnam.

s: Where is Agnishodh, the Indian Army Research Cell inaugurated on 4 Aug 2025, located?
x: Agnishodh is the Indian Army Research Cell at the IIT Madras Research Park.

s: GTRE is developing the marine gas turbine 'Samudra' from which engine?
x: GTRE's marine gas turbine 'Samudra' is derived from the Kaveri engine.

s: Of which fleet of the Indian Navy is Visakhapatnam the home port?
x: Visakhapatnam is home to the Eastern Fleet, where P-17A frigates are commissioned.

s: To which project do Khanderi and Vagir belong?
x: Khanderi and Vagir are Project 75 Kalvari-class Scorpenes built by MDL.

s: Where was India's first indigenous aircraft carrier INS Vikrant (IAC-1) built?
x: INS Vikrant (IAC-1) was built at Cochin Shipyard.

s: Where was the stealth frigate Tavasya built?
x: Tavasya is a stealth frigate from Goa Shipyard.

s: India's two defence industrial corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and which other state?
x: The corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu; the BrahMos unit at Lucknow is linked with the UP corridor.

s: With which of the following is NSTL, Visakhapatnam, DRDO's naval weapons laboratory, associated?
o: Torpedoes such as Varunastra, mines and AUVs
x: NSTL is DRDO's naval weapons laboratory, associated with torpedoes such as Varunastra, mines and AUVs.

s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh defence units is correctly matched with its purpose?
o: BEL Palasamudram – Opto-electronics and night vision
Rambilli – New Eastern Naval Command base for submarines
BEL Machilipatnam – Missile and radar systems integration
Naval Dockyard, Visakhapatnam – Missile and radar systems integration
x: Rambilli is the new ENC submarine base. BEL Palasamudram integrates missile and radar systems, BEL Machilipatnam makes opto-electronics and the Naval Dockyard is the ENC refit yard.

s: Which of the following is a node of the Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor?
x: Tamil Nadu's nodes are Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem and Tiruchirappalli.

s: How many nodes does the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor have?
x: The UP corridor has six nodes: Agra, Aligarh, Chitrakoot, Jhansi, Kanpur and Lucknow; Tamil Nadu has five.

s: Where is the BrahMos unit of the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor located?
x: The BrahMos unit is at Lucknow in the UP corridor.

s: Which of the following pairs about defence industrial corridors is correctly matched?
x: UPEIDA is the UP nodal agency; TIDCO and Hosur belong to Tamil Nadu, Jhansi to Uttar Pradesh.

s: In what does BEL's unit at Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh, specialise?
o: Refit of Eastern Naval Command ships
x: BEL Machilipatnam makes opto-electronics / night vision; BEL Palasamudram integrates missiles and radars.

s: The BEL Palasamudram complex for missile and radar systems integration is in which district?
x: BEL Palasamudram is in Sri Sathya Sai district.

s: What is being set up at Rambilli in Anakapalli district?
x: Rambilli is the new ENC submarine base, including for nuclear boats.

s: When was iDEX launched by the Prime Minister?
x: iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) was launched in April 2018.

s: How many Positive Indigenisation Lists, barring imports of listed items after set dates, have been issued?
x: Five Positive Indigenisation Lists have been issued; the SRIJAN portal supports indigenisation.

s: At whom is VIMARSH 2026, offering direct funding, incubation, test-facility access and source-code sharing, aimed?
x: VIMARSH 2026 provides direct funding, incubation and test-facility access for MSMEs and start-ups, and includes source-code sharing.

s: Which of the following set up the Defence Innovation Organisation, the not-for-profit that runs iDEX?
x: The DIO was set up by HAL and BEL, not DRDO; iDEX was launched in April 2018.

s: ADITI, under the iDEX framework, is intended primarily to fund deep-tech start-ups working in which areas?
o: Artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, hypersonics and directed energy
Conventional banking, insurance and retail technology
Agriculture, biotechnology, textiles and food processing
Mining, ports, railways and urban transport
x: ADITI funds deep-tech start-ups in artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, hypersonics and directed energy, with emphasis on critical and strategic defence technologies.

s: Which organisation executes the Technology Development Fund (TDF) of the Ministry of Defence?
x: TDF is executed by DRDO and gives grants of up to Rs 50 crore; the DIO (HAL + BEL) runs iDEX.

s: Under the Defence India Startup Challenge (DISC) of iDEX, who sets the problem statements for start-ups?
x: DISC comprises iDEX challenge rounds in which the Services set problem statements for start-ups to solve.

s: What is SRIJAN?
o: Start-up challenge set by the Services
x: SRIJAN is the indigenisation portal where DPSUs and Services list import items Indian industry can make.

s: What is the full form of iDEX?
x: iDEX is Innovations for Defence Excellence.

s: The Technology Development Fund gives grants of up to how much per project?
x: TDF, executed by DRDO, gives up to ₹50 crore per project.

s: Which firm developed the TDF-funded green propulsion system proved in orbit on PSLV-C58?
x: Bengaluru start-up Bellatrix Aerospace built the 1N green monopropellant thruster, proved on PSLV-C58 (POEM).

s:
Consider the following statements about defence innovation funding:
1. iDEX is run by DIO, set up by HAL and BEL.
2. The TDF is executed by DIO.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: DIO (HAL + BEL) runs iDEX; the Technology Development Fund is executed by DRDO.

s: With which company are the Swathi Weapon Locating Radar and Akash control centres associated?
x: Swathi Weapon Locating Radar and Akash control centres are associated with Bharat Electronics Limited.

s: Where does HAL licence-build the Russian-designed Su-30MKI?
x: HAL licence-builds the Su-30MKI at Nashik; the T-90 Bhishma is licence-built at HVF Avadi.

s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of indigenous designs?
o: ATAGS, Arjun, Tejas, Akash and Pinaka
x: ATAGS, Arjun, Tejas, Akash and Pinaka are identified as indigenous designs. Su-30MKI and T-90 are licence-built, while Akula and F-35 are not made in India.

s: Which of the following is NOT made in India?
x: The Akula submarine was leased from Russia; Su-30 MKI and T-90 are licence-built in India and ATAGS is indigenous.

s:
Consider the following statements about Make in India defence platforms:
1. Su-30 MKI is a licence-built Russian design.
2. ATAGS is an indigenous DRDO-ARDE towed gun.
3. Arjun is a licence-built Russian tank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Su-30 MKI is licence-built at HAL Nashik and ATAGS is indigenous; Arjun is an indigenous DRDO-CVRDE tank.

s: Which company makes the Dhruv Advanced Light Helicopter?
x: Dhruv ALH, like HTT-40, is made by HAL.

s: Which public sector company, set up at Hyderabad in 1970, makes guided missiles such as Akash, Astra and Konkurs?
x: Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL), Hyderabad, makes guided missiles; BEL makes defence electronics and BEML earth movers.

s: What does BEML, a defence public sector company, mainly make?
x: BEML makes earth movers; BDL makes guided missiles and BEL makes defence electronics.

s: In which month and year was the defence sector opened to Indian private participation with foreign direct investment up to 26 per cent under licensing?
x: The defence sector was opened to 100 per cent Indian private participation in May 2001, with FDI up to 26 per cent under the licensing route.

s: In 2021, the 41 factories of the Ordnance Factory Board were regrouped into how many new DPSUs?
x: The 200-year-old OFB was dissolved and its 41 factories regrouped into 7 DPSUs, including Gliders India and Troop Comforts.

s: As what did the Ministry of Defence declare the year 2025?
x: The Ministry of Defence declared 2025 the Year of Reforms and began reviewing DAP 2020 to support JVs and technology transfer for the private sector.

s: Under DAP 2020, offset clauses were dropped in which types of deals?
o: All Indian private-sector deals and all export contracts
x: DAP 2020 dropped offset clauses in government-to-government and single-vendor deals.

s: In which year was the Strategic Partnership (SP) model, in which Indian private firms team up with foreign OEMs, added?
x: The SP model came in 2017; DPP 2016 had added the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category?
o: IDDM stands for Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured
It is the least preferred category under DAP 2020
It was first added in DPP 2016
It was introduced on the advice of the Dhirendra Singh Committee
x: Buy (Indian-IDDM) is the most preferred category under DAP 2020.

s: The Defence Procurement Manual (DPM) 2025, released on 23 October 2025, governs which kind of procurement?
o: Revenue procurement of about Rs 1 lakh crore
Only procurement under the Strategic Partnership model
x: DPM 2025 (released 23 Oct 2025, effective 1 Nov 2025) covers revenue procurement of about Rs 1 lakh crore. Capital acquisition is governed by DAP 2020; exports and the SP model are not what the DPM covers.

s: Which of the following is one of the 7 DPSUs formed from the Ordnance Factory Board in 2021?
x: The 41 OFB factories became 7 DPSUs, including Gliders India and Troop Comforts.

s: In which procurement document was the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category first added?
x: DPP 2016 (Dhirendra Singh committee) first added Buy (Indian-IDDM); 2017 brought the SP model.

s: With reference to the procurement categories under DAP 2020, which one has the HIGHEST priority?
x: Buy (Indian-IDDM) is the highest-priority procurement category under DAP 2020.

s: How many buy categories are there under DAP 2020?
x: DAP 2020 has five buy categories, from Buy (Indian-IDDM) down to Buy (Global).

s:
Consider the following statements about DAP 2020 procurement categories:
1. Buy (Indian-IDDM) has the highest priority.
2. Buy (Global) has the lowest priority.
3. Buy and Make (Indian) ranks above Buy (Indian).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The order is Buy (Indian-IDDM), Buy (Indian), Buy and Make (Indian), Buy (Global – Manufacture in India), Buy (Global).

s: Under DAP 2020, which older category did Buy (Global – Manufacture in India) replace?
x: Buy (Global – Manufacture in India) replaced the old Buy and Make category.

s: Despite record defence exports, which of the following does India still import?
x: India remains outside the top 25 arms exporters and still imports jet engines and defence chips; BrahMos and Astra are exported.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's defence indigenisation?
o: India depends on imported engines and semiconductors
A small share of defence expenditure goes to R&D
Foreign direct investment in defence has been low
India is among the top 25 arms exporters
x: India remains outside the top 25 arms exporters; import dependence, a small R&D share and low FDI are its challenges.

s: Up to what limit is FDI in the defence sector permitted through the automatic route?
x: 74% is allowed through the automatic route; above 74% up to 100% needs the government route where modern technology access is involved.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's defence production and exports?
o: Defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26
DPEPP 2020 targeted Rs 50,000 crore defence exports by 2025
DPEPP 2020 targeted Rs 1.75 lakh crore defence production by 2025
Defence exports rose from Rs 686 crore (2013-14) to Rs 23,622 crore (2024-25)
x: The DPEPP 2020 export target for 2025 was Rs 35,000 crore, not Rs 50,000 crore.

s: Which Indian missile is Indonesia associated with as a buyer?
x: Indonesia is the Astra buyer, the Philippines bought BrahMos, and the UAE is in talks.

s: Through which route is FDI in defence beyond 74% and up to 100% allowed?
x: 74% is automatic; above 74% up to 100% needs the government route.

s: What was India's record defence production in FY 2025-26?
x: Actual FY 2025-26 production was ₹1.78 lakh crore; ₹1.75 lakh crore was the DPEPP target.

s: India's defence exports rose from ₹686 crore in 2013-14 to how much in 2024-25?
x: Exports grew about 34-fold to ₹23,622 crore in 2024-25.

s: What was the defence export target for 2025 under DPEPP 2020?
x: DPEPP 2020 set ₹35,000 crore exports (not ₹50,000 crore) and ₹1.75 lakh crore production.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's defence FDI and exports?
o: 74% FDI is allowed through the automatic route
FDI above 74% is allowed through the automatic route
Exports rose from ₹686 crore (2013-14) to ₹23,622 crore (2024-25)
x: Beyond 74%, FDI up to 100% needs the government route.

s:
Consider the following statements about the energy intensity of GDP:
1. It is the energy used per unit of GDP.
2. A rising value shows growth decoupling from energy use.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Energy intensity is energy used per unit of GDP; it is a falling, not rising, value that shows growth decoupling from energy use.

s: How is peak demand on an electricity grid defined?
o: The average power drawn over a full day
The highest power drawn in a 15-minute interval
The total electricity generated in a month
The maximum annual energy produced by renewable sources
x: Peak demand is the highest power drawn from the grid during a 15-minute interval.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four A's on which energy security rests?
x: The four A's are availability, accessibility, affordability and acceptability. Accumulation is not included.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Energy shortage refers to unmet energy requirement and is expressed in MU.
2. Peak shortage refers to unmet peak demand and is expressed in MW.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Energy shortage is unmet energy requirement (MU or %), while peak shortage is unmet peak demand (MW or %).

s: How many joules does one kilowatt-hour (kWh) of energy equal?
x: 1 kWh is a 1 kW device running for 1 hour = 1,000 W × 3,600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ J; it is the 'unit' on electricity bills.

s: In discussions of conventional energy resources, what does an energy crisis refer to?
o: A rise in electricity consumption during solar hours
A temporary fall in renewable-energy generation only
The danger that fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum may run out
A shortage limited to nuclear fuel imports
x: Energy crisis refers to the danger of exhaustion of fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum.

s:
Consider the following statements about energy terms:
1. Peak demand is the highest draw in a 15-minute interval.
2. A falling energy intensity of GDP shows growth decoupling.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: peak demand is measured over 15-minute intervals, and falling energy per unit GDP means decoupling.

s: Which source supplies approximately 55% of India’s energy mix and over 74% of its power generation?
x: Coal supplies about 55% of the energy mix and more than 74% of power generation.

s: What is India's rank among the world's energy consumers?
x: India is the third-largest energy consumer and the second-largest coal consumer; its energy demand is expected to triple by 2047.

s: India’s per-capita electricity consumption increased from 957 kWh in FY 2014 to approximately what level in FY 2025?
x: Per-capita electricity consumption rose from 957 kWh in FY 2014 to 1,460 kWh in FY 2025.

s: India’s per-capita energy consumption is approximately what fraction of the world average?
x: India’s per-capita energy consumption is reported as only one-third of the world average.

s: Why is the policy objective of raising per-capita electricity consumption linked to the Human Development Index?
o: Electricity consumption is unrelated to social development indicators
Higher electricity consumption automatically eliminates urban-rural disparity
A minimum level of per-capita consumption is needed for a minimally acceptable level of well-being
HDI measures only the availability of commercial energy
x: Per-capita electricity consumption acts as a proxy for energy use, and a certain minimum level is required to ensure a minimally acceptable level of well-being.

s: Which of the following describes India's per-capita energy consumption?
o: Uniform across urban and rural areas
Low, with a large urban-rural disparity
High in rural areas and negligible in urban areas
x: India has low per-capita energy consumption with a large urban-rural gap.

s: By 2040, which sector is projected to remain the largest consumer of energy in India?
x: Industry uses about half of India's electricity and stays the largest consumer by 2040, while cooking demand falls.

s: India's non-fossil share of installed power capacity rose from 32% in 2014 to what level in 2025?
x: It reached 51% in 2025, crossing the 50% target five years early.

s: About what fraction of China's per-capita electricity consumption is India's?
x: It is about one-fifth of China's and one-ninth of the USA's.

s: After fossil fuels, what ranks second in India's energy supply?
x: After fossil fuels, solar is the second source (UPPSC 2021).

s:
Consider the following statements about India's energy demand:
1. India is the third-largest energy consumer in the world.
2. India's energy demand is projected to triple by 2047.
3. India is the largest coal consumer in the world.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India is the third-largest energy consumer and its demand is to triple by 2047; it is the second-largest coal consumer.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's per-capita consumption?
o: Per-capita electricity use is higher than China's
Per-capita electricity is about 1/9 of the USA's
Per-capita electricity rose from 957 kWh (FY14) to 1,460 kWh (FY25)
Per-capita energy is about one-third of the world average
x: India's per-capita electricity is only about 1/5 of China's.

s: What is India's rank among the world's coal consumers?
x: India is the second-largest coal consumer and the third-largest energy consumer in the world.

s: Which sector uses about 50% of India's electricity?
x: Industry, not households, uses about half of India's electricity; household electrification is about 99%.

s: Which of the following are the emerging drivers of India's peak electricity demand?
o: Electric vehicles, farm pumps, appliances, cooling and data centres
Declining appliance ownership and reduced telecom activity
Only household lighting in rural areas
Only coal mining and railway electrification
x: Electric vehicles, farm pumps, appliances, cooling demand, data centres and telecom operations all contribute to rising electricity demand.

s: India's peak electricity demand rose by approximately 37%, from 183 GW in December 2020 to over what level in April 2026?
x: Peak demand increased from 183 GW in December 2020 to more than 250 GW in April 2026, representing a rise of about 37%.

s: Which scheme provided electricity connections to about 26 million households?
x: The Saubhagya programme is associated with connecting approximately 26 million households.

s: Which energy demand in India is projected to fall by 2040?
x: Industry stays the largest consumer; cooking demand falls, while cooling and data centres drive growth.

s: About what share of Indian households is electrified?
x: Household electrification is about 99%; Saubhagya covered about 26 million households.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's electricity shortage?
x: The shortage was 4.2% in FY14; it fell to 0.03% in 2025 and to zero by November 2025.

s: What is Delhi's response to the 6–11 p.m. evening electricity peak, caused by cooling demand after solar output drops?
x: Delhi uses time-of-day tariffs and smart meters to manage the evening peak.

s: India's aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses declined from 22.62% in FY14 to approximately what level in FY25?
x: AT&C losses fell from 22.62% in FY14 to 15.04% in FY25, alongside measures such as RDSS, IPDS, smart meters and time-of-day tariffs. 10.04%, 18.62% and 12.50% are not the reported FY25 figure.

s: To which hours was India's electricity deficit confined on 25 April 2026?
x: There was no solar-hour shortage; a 2% non-solar deficit made the evening peak the focus of storage.

s: By about how much was India's record peak demand of 270.8 GW in May 2026 higher than in 2019?
x: The 270.8 GW record (May 2026) was about 90 GW above 2019.

s: Why may regional imbalances in renewable electricity arise in India?
x: Poor storage and slow transmission can strand renewable power in some regions, while heatwaves add stress on grids.

s: Why has the evening peak become central to India's storage push?
o: Renewable energy cannot contribute during daylight hours
Coal supplies less than one-tenth of power generation
The remaining deficit occurs mainly during non-solar evening hours
Electricity demand is highest only during solar hours
x: Although solar-hour supply has improved, the non-solar evening peak still creates a deficit, making storage important for meeting that period’s demand.

s: The annual publication titled “Energy Statistics” is brought out by which organisation?
o: Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Power
Central Statistics Office, now functioning as the National Statistics Office under MoSPI
x: Energy Statistics was published by the Central Statistics Office (CSO), now the National Statistics Office (NSO) under MoSPI.

s: Which ministry launched the India Cooling Action Plan in 2019?
x: MoEFCC launched it in 2019; it aims to cut cooling demand by 20–25% and refrigerant demand by 25–30% by 2037–38.

s: Which of the following report – publisher pairs is correctly matched?
o: Electric Power Survey – Central Electricity Authority
India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 – International Energy Agency
x: The Electric Power Survey is CEA's demand forecast. IESS 2047 is NITI Aayog's, the India Energy Outlook is the IEA's and Energy Statistics is published by CSO, now NSO.

s: Which organisation publishes the World Energy Outlook?
x: The IEA publishes it; WEO 2022 projected India's coal generation and oil imports to peak around 2030.

s: What peak power demand by 2035–36 does the CEA's National Generation Adequacy Plan (2026–27 to 2035–36) project?
x: NGAP projects 459 GW peak demand, 1,121 GW installed capacity and 70% non-fossil capacity.

s: As per NITI Aayog's India Energy Security Scenarios, by how much was India's energy demand expected to rise between 2012 and 2040?
x: Total energy demand was projected to rise 2.7–3.2 times from 2012 to 2040, while electricity demand would rise 4.5-fold.

s: With reference to NITI Aayog's 'Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero', which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Renewables' share of generation by 2070 – about 80%
Renewables' share of generation in 2024-25 – about 50%
Coal's share of generation in 2024-25 – about 20%
Coal's share of generation by 2070 – about 80%
x: NITI Aayog's net-zero scenarios see renewables giving about 80% of power generation by 2070. Today coal, not renewables, gives over 74% of generation, and coal's share falls sharply by 2070.

s: What was India's all-time high peak electricity demand recorded in May 2026?
x: The May 2026 peak demand was an all-time high of 270.8 GW, about 90 GW above the 2019 level.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the coverage of India's Energy Statistics publication?
o: Coal, lignite, crude oil and natural gas, including imports and exports, plus the energy balance
Production data only, excluding imports and exports
Crude oil and natural gas only
x: It covers coal, lignite, crude oil, natural gas, electricity consumption and the energy balance, including imports and exports.

s: As per NITI Aayog's IESS, by how much would India's electricity demand rise between 2012 and 2040?
x: IESS projects electricity demand to rise 4.5-fold; total energy demand 2.7–3.2 times.

s: Which body publishes the Electric Power Survey?
x: The Electric Power Survey and NGAP are CEA reports.

s: Around which year do India's coal generation and oil imports peak, according to the IEA's World Energy Outlook 2022?
x: WEO 2022 sees India's coal generation and oil imports peaking around 2030.

s: By how much does the India Cooling Action Plan aim to cut cooling demand by 2037-38?
x: ICAP targets a 20–25% cut in cooling demand and 25–30% in refrigerant demand.

s: Under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, through which entities do the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and NMEEE promote energy efficiency?
x: BEE and the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency under NAPCC work through ESCOs.

s: Andhra Pradesh's Resource Adequacy Plan (2025–26 to 2035–36) seeks about how much new thermal capacity?
x: The plan seeks about 5,588 MW of new thermal capacity; APERC cleared the first 1,600 MW.

s: Why is nuclear energy significant for India's energy system?
o: Provides 24×7 baseload power and can reduce fossil-fuel imports
x: Nuclear power gives round-the-clock baseload electricity and can cut dependence on fossil-fuel imports.

s: During the 2026 gas crisis, which strait was identified as a risk to India's LPG supplies?
x: The Strait of Hormuz was identified as the risk; India imports about 50–51% of its natural gas/LNG.

s: Which authority has been allowed to import coal under the Andhra Pradesh energy roadmap?
x: APGENCO has been allowed to import coal under the Andhra Pradesh energy roadmap.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's NDC targets (versus 2005)?
o: The first NDC (2015) targeted a 33–35% cut in emission intensity by 2030
The 2031–35 NDC targets 50% non-fossil capacity by 2035
The 2031–35 NDC targets a 47% cut in intensity by 2035
The updated NDC (Aug 2022) targeted a 45% cut in intensity and 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030
x: The 2031–35 NDC sets a 60% non-fossil capacity target, not 50%.

s: The COP31 goal described as “35 by 35” seeks to make electricity account for what share of final energy by 2035?
x: The “35 by 35” goal seeks to raise electricity's share to 35% of final energy by 2035.

s: What is the size of the central VGF battery-storage project with NHPC under Andhra Pradesh's September 2026 energy roadmap?
x: The NHPC VGF project is 500 MW/1,000 MWh; the 1,500 MW/6,000 MWh BESS is planned for the evening peak.

s: Which body issued the Draft National Electricity Policy 2026?
x: It is from the Ministry of Power; it replaces the 2005 policy and proposes 100 GW of pumped storage by 2047.

s: By what percentage below the 2005 level has India's emissions intensity declined?
x: Emissions intensity has declined by 36% below the 2005 level.

s: About what share of India's crude oil is imported?
x: About 88% of crude oil is imported; gas/LNG import dependence is about 50–51%.

s: Which of the following pairs about India's share of world reserves is correctly matched?
x: India has about 7% of coal reserves, 0.4% of oil and 0.6% of gas.

s: By how much does India's updated NDC (Aug 2022) target to cut the emissions intensity of GDP by 2030, versus 2005?
x: The Aug 2022 NDC targets 45% by 2030; 47% is the 2035 target and 36% is already achieved.

s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 targets how much pumped storage by 2047?
x: The draft policy, replacing the 2005 policy, targets 100 GW of pumped storage by 2047.

s: At what level does CEA's Resource Adequacy Plan project Andhra Pradesh's peak demand by 2035-36?
x: AP's peak is projected at 30,927 MW by 2035-36, with about 5,588 MW of new thermal capacity.

s: How much of Andhra Pradesh's new thermal capacity has APERC cleared first?
x: APERC cleared the first 1,600 MW of the planned new thermal capacity.

s: How much battery storage (BESS) does Andhra Pradesh's September 2026 energy roadmap plan?
x: The roadmap plans 1,500 MW/6,000 MWh BESS; the NHPC VGF project is 500 MW/1,000 MWh.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's fuel position?
o: India's crude-oil import dependence is about 88%
India holds about 7% of the world's oil reserves
India has the fifth-largest coal reserves in the world
Coal makes up about 55% of India's primary energy
x: India holds only about 0.4% of world oil reserves; 7% is its share of coal reserves. India has the fifth-largest coal reserves, imports about 88% of its crude oil, and coal is about 55% of its energy mix.

s: What non-fossil share of installed capacity does India's NDC for 2031–35 set?
x: The 2031–35 NDC raises the non-fossil capacity target to 60% (the 2022 NDC had 50%).

s: About what share of India's natural gas (LNG) need is met by imports?
x: About half of India's gas is imported as LNG, while about 88% of crude oil is imported.

s: Under which plan is the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE) one of the missions?
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)
x: NMEEE is one of the missions under the NAPCC and is run with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.

s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 of the Ministry of Power replaces the National Electricity Policy of which year?
x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the 2005 policy.

s: Which of the following energy sources is NOT derived from the Sun?
x: Geothermal energy comes from the Earth's interior heat; tidal and nuclear energy are the other sources not derived from the Sun.

s:
Consider the following statements about the classification of energy resources:
1. Hydro power is both conventional and renewable.
2. 'Conventional' energy means non-renewable energy.
3. Tidal energy is not derived from the Sun.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 'Conventional' means long-established use, not non-renewable, so hydro and biomass are conventional and renewable; tidal energy comes from the movement of ocean water.

s: What is India's rank in the world in coal reserves?
x: India has the world's fifth-largest coal reserves, though it is the second-largest coal producer.

s: Of India's 26 sedimentary basins, how many are producing hydrocarbons?
x: India has 26 sedimentary basins, of which only 7 are producing.

s: India has about 17% of the world's population. Approximately what share of the world's oil reserves does it hold?
x: India holds only about 0.4% of world oil reserves. 0.6% is its share of gas reserves and 7% its share of coal reserves; 4% is not a stated figure.

s: Which State has India's largest monazite (thorium) resources?
x: Andhra Pradesh leads with 3.72 Mt of monazite, followed by Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Kerala and West Bengal.

s: The large low-grade uranium deposit at Tummalapalle is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Tummalapalle, a large low-grade uranium deposit, is in YSR Kadapa district.

s: What is India's rank among the world's coal producers?
x: India is the second-largest coal producer, though it has only the fifth-largest coal reserves.

s: Which country is a key supplier of LNG to India?
x: Qatar is identified as a key LNG supplier to India.

s: What is India's import dependence for lithium?
x: Lithium import dependence is about 90%; crude oil is about 88% and coal about 26%.

s: What is India's rank among the world's oil consumers in 2026?
x: India is the third-largest oil consumer and also the third-largest energy consumer in the world. Second, fourth and fifth are incorrect.

s: Which of the following pairs of supplier and approximate share of India's crude imports in 2025 is correctly matched?
x: In 2025 Russia supplied about 35% of India's crude imports, Iraq about 20%, Saudi Arabia about 15% and the US about 8%.

s: About what share of global oil does OPEC produce?
x: OPEC produces about 40% of global oil; its share of India's crude imports has fallen below 50%.

s: On which of the following does India's LPG supply mainly depend?
o: Underground storage maintained by state governments alone
x: India’s LPG supply depends mainly on stocks held by oil marketing companies. Semi-strategic underground LPG storage is only about 0.14 MT.

s: By August 2025, to what level had OPEC's share of India's crude-oil imports fallen?
x: OPEC's share of India's crude imports fell below 50% (Aug 2025), though OPEC still produces about 40% of global oil.

s: Which country has been India's largest crude-oil supplier in recent years?
x: Russia was the largest supplier; Iraq and Saudi Arabia were also major suppliers.

s: About what share of India's coal requirement is imported, even though India is the second-largest coal producer?
x: India imports about 26% of its coal despite being the world's second-largest producer.

s: According to PPAC provisional data (July 2026), about what share of India's crude oil requirement is imported?
x: PPAC provisional data put India's crude oil import dependence at about 88.5%.

s: After the Strait of Hormuz closure in March 2026, India proposed a strategic fuel system of what capacity?
x: The disruption was linked to a 41% jump in the July crude bill, an LPG crunch and a proposed 41 MT strategic fuel system.

s: Roughly what share of world crude-oil trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz?
x: About 15 million bbl/day, roughly 34% of world crude trade, passes through it, along with about a fifth of global LNG trade.

s: Between which countries does the Strait of Hormuz lie?
x: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and carries about 34% of world crude trade.

s: Which is the biggest driver of India's trade deficit and current account deficit?
x: Oil imports are the biggest driver of India's trade deficit and CAD, so global price volatility also feeds domestic inflation.

s: With which macroeconomic effects in India is a rise in international oil prices most directly associated?
o: A rise in exports and elimination of the current account deficit
Lower inflation and a narrower trade deficit
A wider trade deficit and higher inflation
A fall in import expenditure and currency appreciation
x: Higher oil prices increase import costs, thereby widening the trade deficit and contributing to inflation.

s: What was India's crude-oil import bill in FY 2024-25?
x: The crude import bill in FY 2024-25 was $137.0 billion, up 3%; $13.7 billion is the bill for July 2026 alone.

s: In cooking applications, which fuels can methanol partly replace?
x: Methanol, a low-carbon hydrogen-carrier fuel, can partly replace LPG and kerosene in cooking, besides petrol/diesel in transport.

s: Imports of which fuel does the Compressed Biogas Obligation in the City Gas Distribution sector mainly aim to substitute?
x: The CBO is intended to promote compressed biogas and substitute LNG imports.

s: What share of CNG-PNG is the Compressed Biogas Obligation set at from FY 2028-29?
x: The obligation is 1% in FY26, 3% in FY27, 4% in FY28 and 5% from FY 2028-29.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's E20 ethanol-blended petrol:
1. The E20 blending target was advanced to ESY 2025-26 from 2030.
2. E20 petrol with a minimum 91 RON has been mandated from 1 April 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The E20 target was advanced from 2030 to ESY 2025-26; the mandate from 1 April 2026 is for E20 with a minimum 95 RON, not 91.

s: How is Di-Methyl Ether (DME) obtained from two methanol molecules?
x: DME is two methanol molecules minus one water molecule; it can substitute propane in LPG and diesel in slow-RPM engines.

s: Which fuel can Di-Methyl Ether (DME) replace under the Methanol Economy programme?
x: DME replaces propane in LPG and diesel in slow-RPM engines, not petrol.

s: In which fuel is 15% methanol blended in the M15 blend?
x: M15 is 15% methanol in petrol, cutting petrol/crude imports by at least 15%.

s: Blending 20% DME in LPG is estimated to save India about how much a year?
x: 20% DME blending in LPG saves about ₹6,000 crore a year, or ₹50–100 per cylinder.

s: When did India's Ethanol Blended Petrol programme begin with 5% blending?
x: 5% EBP began in January 2003 in 9 sugarcane States and 4 UTs, including Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of NITI Aayog's Methanol Economy programme?
o: Converting coal reserves and municipal solid waste into methanol
Increasing imports of LPG for cooking
x: The Methanol Economy aims to cut the oil import bill, cut GHG emissions and turn coal and municipal waste into methanol; methanol is meant to replace part of LPG, not raise its imports.

s: Which body is driving the Methanol Economy programme in India?
x: The Methanol Economy programme is driven by NITI Aayog.

s: By at least how much is M15 blending (15% methanol in petrol) expected to cut India's petrol or crude imports?
x: M15 is expected to cut petrol/crude imports by at least 15% and PM, NOx and SOx by about 20%.

s: What do companies get under the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP)?
o: Separate licences for oil and for gas
A single licence for all hydrocarbons
x: HELP provides a single, unified licence for all hydrocarbons; OALP concerns upstream exploration and production.

s: In which year was Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 adopted by the Government of India?
x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 was adopted by the Government of India in 2000.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a focus area associated with Hydrocarbon Vision 2025?
o: Complete prohibition of private participation in hydrocarbons
x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 promotes a free market and competition; it does not seek complete prohibition of private participation. The other three are stated focus areas.

s: Which company, the overseas arm of ONGC, acquires equity oil and gas abroad for India?
x: ONGC Videsh (OVL) is ONGC's overseas arm and buys equity oil and gas abroad.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: HELP – Single licence for all hydrocarbons
ONGC Videsh – Retail marketing of LPG in India
x: ONGC Videsh buys equity oil and gas abroad; it is not an LPG marketing company.

s:
Consider the following statements about Hydrocarbon Vision 2025:
1. It was adopted in 2000.
2. It bans private participation in the hydrocarbon sector.
3. It seeks self-reliance through indigenous production and equity oil abroad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 (2000) promotes self-reliance, free market and competition; it does not ban private players.

s: What is the full form of OALP in India's upstream oil and gas sector?
x: OALP, the Open Acreage Licensing Policy, offers blocks for upstream exploration and production under HELP.

s: Which of the following pairs are import-substitution tools in India's energy sector?
o: Green Hydrogen Mission and the proposed 41 MT strategic fuel system
500 GW non-fossil target and the proposed 41 MT strategic fuel system
The proposed 41 MT strategic fuel system alone
500 GW non-fossil capacity target by 2030 and the Green Hydrogen Mission
x: The 500 GW target and the Green Hydrogen Mission are the import-substitution tools; the 41 MT strategic fuel system is a response to energy disruption.

s: Which scheme did PM E-DRIVE, in force from 1 October 2024, replace?
x: PM E-DRIVE (₹10,900 crore) replaced FAME-II and has been extended to March 2028.

s: When did India become an association country of the International Energy Agency?
x: India has been an IEA association country since March 2017 and sought full membership in October 2023.

s: Besides India, which countries are the core founding members of the Global Biofuels Alliance, launched at the G20 New Delhi summit?
x: The Global Biofuels Alliance (9 Sep 2023) was founded by India, the USA and Brazil; its secretariat is in New Delhi.

s: Where is the secretariat of the Global Biofuels Alliance, launched at the G20 New Delhi summit in 2023?
x: The Global Biofuels Alliance, launched on 9 September 2023 by India, the USA and Brazil, has its secretariat in New Delhi.

s: What is the outlay of the PM E-DRIVE scheme, which replaced FAME-II from 1 October 2024?
x: PM E-DRIVE, in force from 1 October 2024, has an outlay of ₹10,900 crore and replaced FAME-II.

s: Which body released the India Electric Mobility Index in August 2025?
x: NITI Aayog released the India Electric Mobility Index on 4 August 2025.

s: Where is the secretariat of the International Energy Forum (IEF) located?
x: The IEF, the largest grouping of energy ministers, has its secretariat in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

s: In which city did India host the 16th International Energy Forum Ministerial in April 2018?
x: India hosted the 16th IEF Ministerial in New Delhi in April 2018; it was inaugurated by the PM.

s: KABIL, set up in 2019 under the Ministry of Mines, is a joint venture of which companies?
x: KABIL is a JV of NALCO, Hindustan Copper (HCL) and MECL.

s: In which province of Argentina are KABIL's five lithium blocks located?
x: KABIL signed for five lithium blocks in Catamarca, Argentina, on 15 Jan 2024.

s: What is the total outlay of the National Critical Mineral Mission, approved in January 2025?
x: The mission has ₹34,300 crore over seven years: ₹16,300 crore from government and ₹18,000 crore from PSUs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Phase I Strategic Petroleum Reserves?
o: They are underground rock caverns at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur
Their capacity is 5.33 MMT, about 9.5 days of cover when full
The IEA norm for strategic reserves is 60 days of cover
Actual stocks of about 3.37 MT give only about 5 days of cover
x: The IEA norm is 90 days of cover, not 60.

s: What is the capacity of the strategic petroleum reserve at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Visakhapatnam reserve has a stated capacity of 1.33 MMT; Padur (Karnataka) has 2.5 MMT.

s: Which is the largest of India's Phase I Strategic Petroleum Reserves?
x: Padur (2.5 MMT) is the largest Phase I site, ahead of Mangaluru (1.5 MMT) and Visakhapatnam (1.33 MMT); Chandikhol is a Phase II site.

s: In which state is Chandikhol, an approved Phase II Strategic Petroleum Reserve site, located?
x: Phase II approved sites are Chandikhol (Odisha) and Padur (Karnataka); Bikaner (Rajasthan) and Rajkot (Gujarat) are proposed.

s: Which Strategic Petroleum Reserve site figures in both Phase I and Phase II?
x: Padur in Karnataka is the only site in both Phase I and Phase II.

s: How many days of cover does the International Energy Agency norm for strategic oil stocks require?
x: The IEA norm is 90 days of cover, against only about 5 days from India's SPRs.

s: In which state are the Mangaluru and Padur Strategic Petroleum Reserves located?
x: Both Mangaluru (1.5 MMT) and Padur (2.5 MMT) SPRs are in Karnataka.

s: Which of the following pairs of Strategic Petroleum Reserve site and state is correctly matched?
x: Bikaner (Rajasthan) and Rajkot (Gujarat) are proposed SPR sites; Chandikhol is in Odisha and Padur in Karnataka.

s: Where is the Krishna-Godavari Basin, one of India's most prolific hydrocarbon zones, located?
x: The KG Basin is an offshore East Coast zone, where Andhra Pradesh produces gas and crude oil.

s: In which year was the Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy (IIPE), Visakhapatnam, established in 2016, declared an Institution of National Importance?
x: IIPE was established in 2016, became an Institution of National Importance in 2017 and signed a shale-modelling pact with OIL India in April 2026.

s: Which company is the operator of the KG-D6 block in the Krishna-Godavari Basin?
x: Reliance operates KG-D6 with a 66.67% share; BP holds 33.33%, and ONGC runs the neighbouring KG-DWN-98/2 block.

s: Which company runs the oil refinery at Visakhapatnam, which also hosts a Phase I SPR?
x: Visakhapatnam has the HPCL refinery and a 1.33 MMT Phase I Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

s: Which company operates the KG-DWN-98/2 deepwater block next to KG-D6 in the Krishna-Godavari Basin?
x: KG-DWN-98/2 is an ONGC deepwater block; KG-D6 is run by Reliance with BP.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Energy Transition Index — World Economic Forum
State Energy and Climate Index — International Energy Agency
National Generation Adequacy Plan — NITI Aayog
India Energy Outlook — Bureau of Energy Efficiency
x: The Energy Transition Index is published by the World Economic Forum. The State Energy and Climate Index is by NITI Aayog, the National Generation Adequacy Plan by CEA, and India Energy Outlook by the IEA.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Energy Agency (IEA)?
x: The IEA is headquartered in Paris; Abu Dhabi hosts IRENA, Vienna hosts OPEC and Gurugram hosts the International Solar Alliance.

s: Who prepared the National Generation Adequacy Plan 2026-27 to 2035-36?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: The National Generation Adequacy Plan is prepared by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA).

s: Who publishes the Energy Transition Index?
x: The Energy Transition Index is the World Economic Forum's.

s: In January 2020, the International Energy Agency, along with NITI Aayog, released which of the following?
o: The first in-depth review of India's energy policies
The State Energy and Climate Index
x: The IEA released its first in-depth review of India's energy policies in January 2020 with NITI Aayog. The Energy Transition Index is by WEF; the State indices are by NITI Aayog and BEE.

s: Which organisation, along with NITI Aayog, prepared the first in-depth review of India's energy policies?
x: The first in-depth review of India's energy policies (2020) was prepared by the International Energy Agency with NITI Aayog.

s: Who jointly brought out the report 'Renewables Integration in India 2021'?
x: Renewables Integration in India 2021 was published by NITI Aayog together with the International Energy Agency.

s: Who publishes the State Energy Efficiency Index?
x: The State Energy Efficiency Index is brought out by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency with AEEE; the State Energy and Climate Index is by NITI Aayog.

s:
Match the following organisations with their headquarters:
List-I (Organisation)
A. IEA
B. IRENA
C. OPEC
D. International Solar Alliance
List-II (Headquarters)
1. Vienna
2. Gurugram
3. Paris
4. Abu Dhabi
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: IEA is in Paris, IRENA in Abu Dhabi, OPEC in Vienna and the International Solar Alliance in Gurugram.

s:
Consider the following statements about The Climate Group:
1. It is a nonprofit organisation.
2. It was founded in 2003.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Climate Group is a nonprofit founded in 2003, so both statements are correct.

s: Who publishes the India Energy Outlook report?
x: The India Energy Outlook, like the World Energy Outlook, is published by the IEA (HQ Paris).

s: Under the Electricity Act, 2003, who fixes Renewable Purchase Obligations?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: The Electricity Act 2003 enables State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations.

s: The energy-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 are intended to feed into which mechanism?
o: The National Green Hydrogen Mission alone
The State Energy and Climate Index
x: Greenhouse-gas emission-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act 2001 feed into the domestic carbon market.

s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 proposes how much pumped storage hydropower capacity by 2047?
x: It proposes 100 GW of pumped storage by 2047, along with Time-of-Day tariffs.

s: What is a household called that has rooftop solar and battery storage, uses part of its power and sells the surplus to the grid?
x: A consumer who also produces or stores electricity is a prosumer; DERs turn consumers into prosumers.

s: Under the Renewable Purchase Obligation, which entities must buy a prescribed share of power from renewable sources?
o: DISCOMs and open-access or captive users
x: RPO requires DISCOMs and open-access or captive users to buy a prescribed share of renewable power; SERCs fix the obligation.

s: By which date must solar and wind projects be commissioned to get the 100% ISTS charge waiver?
x: The full waiver covers projects commissioned by 30 June 2025; it is then graded, with a 75% waiver to June 2026.

s: In which year was the Tariff Policy of 2006 revised?
x: The Tariff Policy, required by the Electricity Act 2003, dates from 2006 and was revised in 2016.

s: Which of the following set consists entirely of distributed energy resources?
o: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV
Large hydropower dams, coal plants, fuel cells and refineries
Battery storage, oil terminals, nuclear reactors and rooftop solar PV
Coal mines, biomass generators, gas pipelines and fuel cells
