x: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV all qualify as distributed energy resources.

s: By how much does India's new NDC (2031-35) aim to cut the emissions intensity of GDP by 2035?
x: The new NDC targets a 47% intensity cut and 60% non-fossil capacity by 2035; 45% and 50% are the 2030 targets.

s: How much non-fossil power capacity does India aim to reach by 2030 under the Panchamrit targets?
x: Panchamrit targets 500 GW non-fossil capacity, 50% energy from renewables, 1 billion tonnes less emissions and 45% lower carbon intensity by 2030, and net zero by 2070.

s: At which conference did India submit its Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy to the UNFCCC?
x: India submitted its Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy to the UNFCCC at COP27 in 2022.

s: At which conference were India's Panchamrit commitments announced?
x: Panchamrit was announced at COP26, Glasgow (2021); the Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy came at COP27.

s: Under India's updated NDC (2022), what is the target share of non-fossil installed power capacity by 2030?
x: The 2022 NDC targets 50% non-fossil capacity and a 45% intensity cut by 2030; 60% is the 2035 target.

s: By 2026, non-fossil sources made up about what share of India's installed power capacity?
x: Non-fossil capacity reached 52.27% in 2026, and renewables crossed 200 GW.

s: Under the Panchamrit commitments made at COP26, what share of India's energy requirement is to come from renewable energy by 2030?
x: Panchamrit target 2 is that 50% of India's energy requirement will come from renewables by 2030 (not 60%).

s: By which year does India aim to achieve net zero emissions?
x: India's net-zero target year, announced as part of Panchamrit at COP26, is 2070. Andhra Pradesh aims for 2047.

s: Under the Panchamrit commitments announced at COP26, by how much is India to cut its projected cumulative carbon emissions by 2030?
x: Panchamrit target 3: cut projected cumulative emissions by 1 billion tonnes by 2030.

s: By how much did India's updated NDC (2022) commit to reduce the emissions intensity of its GDP by 2030 over the 2005 level?
x: The updated NDC (2022) set a 45% cut in emissions intensity by 2030 over 2005; 47% is the new target for 2035.

s: India’s stated goal of achieving energy independence is associated with which year?
x: India has set the goal of achieving energy independence by 2047. Net zero emissions is the separate 2070 target.

s: Who prepared the Draft National Energy Policy (2017)?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
x: National Energy Policy is NITI Aayog's; the National Electricity Policy (2005) is the Ministry of Power's.

s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy of which year?
x: Issued by the Ministry of Power, it replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005.

s: Who chaired the Planning Commission Expert Committee that prepared the Integrated Energy Policy (2006)?
x: The Integrated Energy Policy was drafted by the Planning Commission's Expert Committee chaired by Kirit Parikh, reported in 2006 and was approved by the Cabinet in December 2008. The other economists did not chair this committee.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's electricity policies?
o: The Electricity Act 2003 requires a National Electricity Policy and a Tariff Policy
The Tariff Policy of 2006 was revised in 2016
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 was issued by NITI Aayog
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005
x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 comes from the Ministry of Power, not NITI Aayog.

s: Which of the following document – drafting body pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Draft National Energy Policy (2017) – NITI Aayog
Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 – NITI Aayog
National Electricity Policy (2005) – Ministry of Power
x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 is from the Ministry of Power; the Draft National Energy Policy is NITI Aayog's.

s: When was the Integrated Energy Policy, prepared in 2006, approved by the Union Cabinet?
x: It was approved in December 2008 and aimed to meet energy needs up to 2031–32.

s: What did the Integrated Energy Policy recommend for the pricing of tradable fuels?
o: Free pricing only for imported products
A universal price subsidy irrespective of income
x: It recommended market-determined or trade-parity pricing for tradable fuels, with subsidies targeted to the poor.

s: What did the Integrated Energy Policy recommend on fuel subsidies?
o: A general price subsidy for all consumers
x: It recommended subsidies targeted to the poor, with trade-parity pricing, not a general price subsidy.

s: When were diesel prices in India deregulated?
x: Diesel was deregulated in October 2014; petrol in June 2010.

s: When were petrol prices in India deregulated?
x: Petrol was deregulated in June 2010 and diesel in October 2014.

s: With which of the following is PAHAL (2015) related?
o: LPG subsidy through Direct Benefit Transfer
x: PAHAL (2015) delivers the LPG subsidy through DBT.

s: Up to which year did the Integrated Energy Policy aim to meet the energy needs of all at least cost?
x: Its aim was to meet energy needs of all at least cost, reliably and sustainably, till 2031-32.

s: In which year was NITI Aayog's India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 (IESS 2047) launched?
x: IESS 2047 was launched in 2014; 2017 is the year of the Draft National Energy Policy.

s: Fossil fuels account for nearly what share of India's commercial primary energy supply?
x: Fossil fuels constitute nearly 90% of commercial primary energy supply and are increasingly imported.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of NITI Aayog's Draft National Energy Policy?
o: Access to energy at affordable prices
Greater dependence on imported fossil fuels
x: Its objectives are affordable access, improved security and independence, greater sustainability and economic growth; more import dependence runs against the independence objective.

s: Which of the following pairs about nuclear capacity recommended by NITI Aayog's 'Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero' (Feb 2026) is correctly matched?
x: The study recommends 200–300 GW of nuclear capacity by 2070 and about 100 GW by 2047.

s: Which two scenarios does NITI Aayog's India Energy Security Scenarios (IESS) 2047 model?
x: IESS 2047 is NITI Aayog's open-access tool that models energy supply and demand to 2047 under Business-As-Usual and Ambitious scenarios.

s: Which sector does the PNGRB, set up under its 2006 Act, regulate?
x: PNGRB regulates petroleum and natural gas under MoPNG.

s: On which date did the Ministry of Power, earlier the Ministry of Energy Sources, become an independent ministry?
x: It became independent on 2 July 1992; oil and gas belong to MoPNG.

s: Under which entry of the Constitution is 'Electricity' placed?
x: Electricity is a concurrent subject, placed under Entry 38 of List III.

s: In which year did the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy get the name MNRE?
x: It began as DNES in 1982, became MNES in 1992 and was renamed MNRE in 2006.

s: Under whom does the Department of Atomic Energy function directly?
o: The Ministry of Science and Technology
x: The Department of Atomic Energy, handling nuclear power and research, is directly under the Prime Minister.

s: Under which law was the Bureau of Energy Efficiency created?
x: BEE was created under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, and runs NMEEE under the NAPCC.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated missions of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy?

slow electrification always reduces grid volatility
fuel subsidies cause a permanent fall in renewable generation
